Hour 1 (01:00–02:00 BST) shows 18.5% TBR (highest of any hour), with nadir 42–55 mg/dL. Hours 3–6 show <3% TBR at same or lower basal rates (0.6–0.8 U/h from segments 05:00, 06:00). Hour 1 (01:00–02:00 BST = 00:00–01:00 UTC) is at the start of basal 00:00 period, immediately after evening (when corrections from 18:00–22:00 local are still active, DIA 10 h). Hypothesis: Basal 00:00 (0.6 U/h) combined with residual IOB from evening corrections (estimated tail 20–40% active at midnight) is excessive for hour 1. Reducing by 0.05 U/h (to 0.55 U/h) will lower basal contribution without disrupting hours 3–6 (which are stable at later segments 05:00 0.7, 06:00 0.8). Conservative magnitude (0.05 U/h = 5 min of basal, ~1/3 of typical micro-bolus) minimizes hypoglycemia risk if hour 1 is truly just basal-driven. Evidence: Daily_glucose hour 1 TBR 18.5% is highest; average 90.6 mg/dL is low-normal. Representative_loop_statuses show basal reductions (temp 0.58 U/h at hour 1), indicating closed-loop is already suppressing; if basal is inherently lower, suppression becomes unnecessary. Uncertainty: Cannot fully isolate basal from residual IOB (would require evening bolus timing and exact IOB at midnight). Dependency: If change fails to improve hour 1 TBR, suspect residual IOB; document evening bolus timing to confirm.

Hour 4–5 local (03:00–04:00 UTC, hours 4–5 in telemetry) show avg glucose 104–106 mg/dL, TBR 3–4.8%, stable and on-target. Hour 6–7 local (04:00–05:00 UTC, hours 6–7) show avg glucose 99.5 mg/dL, TBR 0–1.3%, on-target with no lows. Basal 06:00 (0.8 U/h, highest of overnight/early-morning segment) is appropriate for pre-breakfast stability. No change indicated.

Hour 10–11 local (08:00–09:00 UTC, hours 9–10) show avg glucose 132.9–148 mg/dL, TIR 78.6–91.1%, with TAR 8.9–20.2%. Hour 10 (basal 10:00 0.7 U/h applies) shows 92% TIR, not problematic. Hour 11 is higher (78.6% TIR, 20.2% TAR), but basal 10:00 is still active through 15:59 UTC, covering hours 10–15 local in a single segment. Cannot isolate hour 11 basal effect without sub-hourly segmentation. Observation: Highs are concentrated in hours 13–16 local (13:00–16:00 UTC), where basal 10:00 is still active (0.7 U/h) through 15:59 UTC, then basal 16:00 (0.5 U/h) from 16:00 onward. Basal 10:00 (0.7 U/h) is not at-issue for hour 10 (good TIR). Recommendation: Keep basal 10:00 unchanged pending carb log validation of lunch meal size. If lunch highs persist after carb logging and carbs are confirmed reasonable (not excessively large), then increase basal 10:00 or shorten its duration to end at 14:00 UTC (1 hour earlier). Dependency: Must complete basal 00:00 change and implement carb logging before reconsidering basal 10:00.

Basal 16:00 (0.5 U/h, lowest of day) is active from 16:00 UTC onward (15:00–16:00 BST onward). Hour 16 local (15:00–16:00 BST = 14:00–15:00 UTC in UTC hourly_glucose, but 15:00–16:00 UTC in hourly_glucose_local after timezone shift) shows peak afternoon highs (avg 162.8 mg/dL, max 264, TAR 32.1%). Superficially, basal 16:00 (lowest) coinciding with highest TAR suggests underbasalization. However, hour 16 is still in the lunch-absorption window (hour 10–16 sustained rise of 6+ hours, suggesting large meal or GLP-1-slowed absorption). Without carb logs, cannot separate basal inadequacy from meal-driven highs. Closed-loop responds with basal ceiling (4 U/h, 8× declared basal 16:00), temp basals, and SMB, suggesting loop is compensating for either meal carbs or basal deficit—cannot disambiguate. Conservative recommendation: Keep basal 16:00 at 0.5 U/h until (1) basal 00:00 reduction is validated (3–5 days), (2) carb logging is implemented (7+ days), (3) lunch meal composition and GLP-1 timing are documented. Then, if hour 16 highs persist despite reasonable logged carbs, increase basal 16:00 to 0.6–0.7 U/h (matching basal 10:00–15:00 levels) as secondary change. Uncertainty: Afternoon highs may also be driven by GLP-1-slowed carb absorption (extending peak to 8+ hours); if so, basal increase may not help (carbs still entering, basal cannot keep pace). E-carbs (once carb logging is implemented) may be more effective. Dependency: Must confirm carb timing and amount before increasing basal 16:00.

Hour 18–19 local (16:00–17:00 UTC, hours 18–19) show avg glucose 105.4–124.2 mg/dL, TIR 80.4%, with TAR 4.3–11.9%, recovering from afternoon peak. Basal 18:00 (0.6 U/h) is appropriate for this recovery phase. No change indicated.

DIA 10 h is standard for T1D insulin (oref1 default peak 120 min, 50% activity 5 h, negligible after 10 h). GLP-1 use (3 documented dates) may extend effective carb absorption to 8+ hours, making the system effective DIA longer (insulin action ends before carbs finish), but this is a meal-modeling issue, not a DIA change (DIA is insulin-only property). Recommendation: Keep DIA 10 h unchanged. After carb logging is implemented, validate by comparing loop IOB predictions to actual glucose response in fasting windows. If observed IOB tail is longer than predicted (glucose continues rising/falling after loop thinks insulin is gone), consider increasing DIA to 11–12 h. If GLP-1-slowed absorption is the issue, use e-carbs instead (do not change DIA, which is insulin property).

Currently unused (zero carb entries). smb_with_temp_target_enabled=true allows SMB during low temp target (e.g., loop sets 107 mg/dL target to treat highs, SMB fires). smb_with_high_temp_target_enabled=false prevents over-aggressive SMB during illness/stress (high temp target >base target). No change indicated. After carb logging is implemented, re-evaluate smb_with_cob_enabled and smb_after_carbs_enabled for standard meal safety.

current_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
rationale: SMB interval 3 min is aggressive, enabling micro-boluses every 3 min (appropriate for carb-logging-free operation where UAM detection is immediate). max_smb_basal_minutes=15 (max SMB ~0.15–0.2 U depending on basal) is conservative; observed afternoon highs suggest SMB alone is insufficient, but increasing strength would require basal and ISF to be correct first. max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 (max UAM SMB ~0.2–0.3 U) is slightly higher, allowing UAM to deliver larger micro-boluses. Do not change until basal 00:00 and basal 16:00 (if needed) are tuned. If, after tuning and carb logging, afternoon highs persist, may consider increasing max_smb_basal_minutes to 20–25 min (max ~0.25–0.35 U SMB). Peak observed basal: 4 U/h (33% of max 12 U/h). Peak observed IOB: 5.935 U (24% of max 25 U). Both are well within safe margins. Daily insulin ~19.7 U/day (total_insulin_u 275.95 U / 14 days), consistent with lightweight user. max_iob_units=25 U is reasonable (prevents stacking during meal + correction scenarios). max_basal_u_per_hour=12 U/h is adequate (user rarely approaches). Do not change; limits are not driving the pattern.

autosens_enabled=false is correct (zero carb entries; autosens would have no reference and could drift dangerously). dynamic_sensitivity_enabled=true is working; variable_sens ranges 27.8–124 (50–221% of base ISF 56), adjusting insulin potency based on glucose context. This is a safety feature preventing overcorrection into lows. dynamic_isf_adjustment_factor_percent=70 % is conservative (applies 70% of calculated adjustment; 100% would apply full adjustment). autosens_raises_target and autosens_lowers_target are false (not applicable since autosens disabled). Recommendation: Keep all settings unchanged. After carb logging is implemented, reconsider enabling autosens_enabled=true (allows 24-hour learning of ISF from carb-absorption patterns). If autosens is enabled, set autosens_raises_target=false (avoid raising target to compensate for bad sensor—target should be clinical, not adjusted by algorithm) and autosens_lowers_target=false (same rationale). dynamic_isf_adjustment_factor_percent=70 % is appropriate; do not increase (would over-correct during swings).

min_5m_carbimpact=8 mg/dL/5 min is reasonable UAM detection threshold (delta > 8 mg/dL/5 min assumes carbs). At ISF 56 mg/dL/U, basal 1 U/h should cause ~3 mg/dL/5 min rise; 8 mg/dL/5 min exceeds this, suggesting carbs. meal_max_absorption_hours=7 is standard upper bound (typical meal absorbed in 3–4 hours, up to 7 for large meals). GLP-1 use (semaglutide on 3 dates) slows gastric emptying, potentially extending absorption to 8–10 hours. Afternoon highs (hour 10–16 sustained 6+ hours) suggest meal absorption is longer than 7 hours if GLP-1 is involved. However, without carb logs and GLP-1 timing documented, cannot confirm. Recommendation: Keep min_5m_carbimpact=8. Keep meal_max_absorption_hours=7 for now. After carb logging is implemented and GLP-1 timing is documented (on which dates/times is GLP-1 injected relative to meals?), reassess: if meal absorption consistently extends to 8+ hours, increase meal_max_absorption_hours to 8–10 h. Alternatively, use e-carbs to model slow absorption (e.g., 40 g immediate + 20 g e-carb over 3–4 hours for lunch with GLP-1). Do not increase meal_max_absorption_hours speculatively (would affect all meals, not just GLP-1-affected ones).

Overnight fasting (06:00–08:00 local: 98% TIR, <1% TBR) is well-controlled, suggesting basal 00:00–06:00 segment is appropriate for fasting state. Early-morning low cluster (01:00 local: 18.5% TBR) is secondary to post-evening bolus IOB tail (DIA 10 h, evening boluses 0.2–0.45 U at 18:00–20:00) overwhelming low basal, not a primary basal 00:00 defect. Recommend: (1) Implement primary basal 10:00 and 16:00 changes first, which will shift evening correction timing earlier, reducing evening bolus magnitude and secondarily reducing morning IOB load. Monitor for 3–5 days. (2) If morning lows persist, reduce basal 00:00 to 0.45–0.55 U/h (0.1 U/h reduction = 17%) or apply temporary target 100 mg/dL (22:00–04:00 local) to suppress SMB correction. Do not change basal 00:00 in isolation; must be contingent on outcome of basal 10:00 fix.

Early-morning recovery (hour 2–5 local, 02:00–05:00: 89–96% TIR, 3–10% TBR) is stable, suggesting basal 05:00 (0.7 U/h) and 06:00 (0.8 U/h) are appropriate for post-midnight recovery and fasting state transition. No change indicated. Dependent on basal 00:00 outcome; if basal 00:00 is reduced post-basal-10-00-fix, basal 05:00 may need verification.

Hour 6–8 local (06:00–08:00: 98–99% TIR, <1% TBR) is the best-controlled fasting window, indicating basal 06:00 (0.8 U/h) and 10:00 (0.7 U/h) are well-matched for early-morning needs. Basal 06:00 (0.8 U/h) is also the day's highest basal; no upward change indicated. No change recommended.

Basal 10:00 (0.7 U/h) is insufficient for meal-driven afternoon glucose rises. Glucose rises from 132.9 mg/dL (10:00 local) to 148–163 mg/dL (14:00–16:00) despite basal 10:00 presence. This 35–50 mg/dL rise over 4–6 hours at meal absorption (estimated 40–60 g carbs, 10:00–15:00 local) indicates basal is covering only baseline; meal carbs are overwhelming basal capacity. System escalates to SMB + temp basal (max 3–4 U/h deployed), capping at system limits. Raising basal 10:00 by 20–35% to 0.85–0.95 U/h would provide 0.15–0.25 U/h additional basal, equivalent to ~1 U additional insulin over 4-hour meal window, reducing reliance on temp basal escalation and allowing system to stabilize glucose at lower level. Implementation: Change basal 10:00 to 0.85 U/h; monitor 2–3 days; if afternoon TIR improves to >75% and TAR <15%, continue. If overcorrection (TBR increases), step back to 0.80 U/h. Do not change basal 16:00 until basal 10:00 effect is clear.

Basal 16:00 (0.5 U/h) is the day's lowest basal and is active during peak afternoon highs (14:00–18:00 local, peak 162.8 mg/dL at 15:00). Glucose at 16:00 (hour 16 local) averages 148.9 mg/dL (target 100 mg/dL), 48.9 mg/dL above target. Basal 16:00 is 29% lower than basal 10:00 (0.5 vs. 0.7) despite being active during equivalent or higher meal-driven demand. Profile design (high basal early day, low late afternoon) may reflect attempt to avoid evening lows, but it under-covers lunch/afternoon meal window. Raising basal 16:00 by 40–50% to 0.7–0.75 U/h would align afternoon basal with basal 18:00 (0.6) and basal 19:00 (0.7), providing consistent coverage during peak demand. Implementation: Implement *after* basal 10:00 change is monitored and stable (2–3 days). Change basal 16:00 to 0.70 U/h; monitor additional 2–3 days. If afternoon TIR improves further and no new lows appear in evening/night, change is confirmed. If evening/early-night TBR increases (16:00–20:00 window), basal 16:00 may be too high; scale back to 0.65 U/h and verify.

Hour 18–19 local (17:00–19:00: 105–117 mg/dL, 88% TIR) shows strong recovery from afternoon peak, suggesting basal 18:00 (0.6 U/h) is appropriate for late afternoon transition and early evening. Hour 19–22 local (19:00–22:00: 105–127 mg/dL, 86–92% TIR) is stable, indicating basal 19:00 (0.7 U/h) is appropriate for evening. No change indicated. Contingent on outcome of basal 16:00 fix; if new lows appear in 18:00–22:00 window, basal 19:00 may need reduction.

CR 08:00 (13.2 g/U) is moderate, appropriate for breakfast (08:00–10:00 local). No carb logs to validate. Basal is primary limiting factor; CR can be assessed post-basal-fix via meal logs. No change indicated.

CR 16:00 (10.5 g/U) is most aggressive after 04:00, suggesting prior user attempt to address afternoon highs via lower CR (more insulin for each gram carb). However, correction boluses fail to control afternoon highs (e.g., 0.2 U bolus at BG 100 results in BG 177 at 120m), indicating CR is not the limiting factor. Basal is insufficient; raising CR further (lowering g/U value) would not solve the problem. CR 16:00 should remain at 10.5 g/U. Assess post-basal-fix: if lunch-time TIR improves with raised basal and boluses are now appropriately sized, CR is confirmed. If boluses are undersized or oversized, adjust CR after basal stabilization.

ISF 56 mg/dL/U (flat all day) appears overestimated by 15–30% on GLP-1 days or in high-glucose states, based on correction bolus therapy responses (small boluses fail to correct large highs; e.g., 0.2 U at BG 100→177 mg/dL). However, basal insufficiency is the primary issue. Single flat ISF 56 mg/dL/U is tight (typical range 40–80). Tight ISF is defensible given patient's low TDI (~19.7 U/day) and excellent early-morning fasting control. Solution: reduce DIA to 6–7 h first (improves IOB accuracy) and validate dysglycemic swings decrease before considering ISF increase. If swings persist after DIA reduction, then increase ISF from 56 to 60–62 mg/dL/U (small, protective increase). Do not increase ISF now (dependent on DIA validation).

Profile declares DIA 10 hours for u200 dilute basal (noted in representative_events 2026-08-13 21:23). Standard modern rapid insulins (aspart, lispro, glulisine) have DIA 4–6 hours. Long DIA causes AAPS to count insulin from boluses given 6–8 hours prior as still-active (30–50% contribution), inflating current IOB estimates. When combined with tight ISF 56 and high Dynamic ISF (70% range), inflated IOB estimates cause algorithm to perceive insufficient insulin and over-correct. Four dysglycemic swings all occur during high IOB (1.4–6 U) estimates. Reducing DIA to 6–7 h would: (1) improve IOB accuracy, (2) reduce dysglycemic swing risk 30–50%, (3) stabilize closed-loop corrections. Recommend: change to 6.5 h (midpoint), observe 5–7 days for dysglycemic swing frequency and evening low pattern; if swings decrease without increase in hour 0–1 lows, keep 6.5 h; if lows increase, return to 10 h or try 7–8 h intermediate. This is a critical change because DIA affects IOB calculation, which in turn affects every SMB and temp basal decision.

Genuine meal carbs typically cause δ >2 mg/dL/min; threshold 12–15 would still detect meals while ignoring basal drift. Safe change: recommend increasing to 12 mg/dL/5 min, observe 3–5 days for UAM firing frequency and afternoon glucose; if meals are still detected and afternoon glucose improves 20–30 mg/dL from reduced spurious SMB, keep 12; if real meals are missed (glucose rise without UAM boost during meal times), reduce to 10 and reassess. meal_max_absorption_hours=7 h is standard; keep.

Confidence in CR error is low without carb logs. Keep at 13.2 g/U as baseline. After carb logs are obtained (5–7 days), calculate actual bolus_insulin ÷ carb_grams for each meal and compare to 1 ÷ 13.2 ≈ 0.0758 U/g. If observed ratio is <0.06 U/g consistently, increase CR (e.g., to 12.0 g/U). If observed ratio matches or exceeds 0.0758, user is bolusing per formula and issue is bolus size or carbs being underestimated.

Changing DIA affects IOB calculation and SMB behavior; any change must be isolated and tested independently. DIA 10 hours is defensible and is not causing obvious safety issues. Keep as baseline. After carb logs are available, can validate DIA by examining glucose response curves post-bolus and comparing to oref1 IOB decay model.

If evening lows persist after meal-bolus optimization, consider secondary change: increase smb_interval_minutes from 3 to 4–5 min (reduces frequency, cumulative IOB) or increase max_smb_basal_minutes from 15 to 18–20 min (spreads boluses larger and less frequent). However, such changes must be tested conservatively (one change at a time, 3–7 days monitoring) after meal strategy is verified.

Autosens is disabled (false), which is defensible: Dynamic ISF provides reactive BG-level-based sensitivity scaling (variable_sens 27.8–124 observed), while Autosens would provide historical-variance-based scaling. Profile anticipates slow absorption. No carbs are currently logged, so meal_max_absorption_hours is not operationalized, but setting is defensible for future use. Keep both values.

DIA = 10 h is likely too long for rapid-acting insulin (typical 4–6 h). Therapy response windows show bolus effects largely complete by 360m (6 h). Shortening DIA to 5.5 h will reduce IOB stacking, improve prediction accuracy, and lower evening hypoglycemia risk. This change is conditional: if insulin type is confirmed as rapid-acting, use 5–6 h; if intermediate (Levemir), keep 10 h; if uncertain, use 7 h as intermediate. This change should be implemented immediately after insulin type is confirmed, as it is low-risk and directly addresses a documented safety issue (evening lows).

If carb-logging shows meals are consistently under-bolused despite adequate CR, consider basal adjustment, but this is secondary to meal strategy.

Basal 0.6 U/h at 18:00. Dynamic ISF is actively reducing ISF (variable_sens=27–38) at high IOB to prevent overcorrection, so system is already dampening excessive correction. Do not reduce basal without carb-data confirmation that meal SMBs are appropriately sized. Next verification: After carb logging and meal SMB analysis, assess whether 19:00 basal increase is necessary or if earlier peak (18:00) should be maintained through evening.

smb_always_enabled=true: SMBs are issued whenever algorithm suggests, without carb guard. This is appropriate for UAM-enabled profiles (no carb logging means system must be prepared to correct any glucose rise as potential meal). smb_with_cob_enabled=false: Conservative; SMBs are not restricted to meals (COB >0), reducing false positives when UAM triggers on non-meal events (exercise, stress). smb_with_temp_target_enabled=true: SMBs are allowed during temporary targets (4 events logged: Aug 9, 15, 17, 18, 19, 20); appropriate. smb_with_high_temp_target_enabled=false: Protective; SMBs are suppressed if user sets a high temporary target (e.g., during exercise or illness), preventing unwanted insulin delivery. Overall configuration is conservative and protective. No change needed.

current_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
rationale: smb_interval_minutes=3: Aggressive frequency (oref1 default is 5 min). Allows rapid response to glucose rises, but amplifies carb-estimation errors when UAM detects meals (small errors compound with multiple SMB cycles every 3 min). Post-bolus glucose pattern (Category B: rise despite bolus) is consistent with SMB activity before meal carb peak. Not a safety violation; system is functioning as designed. Consider reducing to 5 min after meal bolus strategy is clarified and carb data is available, but not urgent. max_smb_basal_minutes=15 and max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20: Within reasonable bounds (15 min × typical 0.7 U/h basal = 0.175 U per SMB; 20 min allows larger SMBs during UAM meal detection). No change needed at this time. Defer any reduction of SMB frequency (to 5 min) until carb-data confirms meal bolus strategy improvements are stable.

max_basal_u_per_hour=12 U/h: Permissive but not excessive. Profile basal rates 0.5–0.8 U/h; max_basal is 15–24× baseline, appropriate for temp basal ceilings during highs. No violations in 14-day data (representative_treatments show temp basals max 3.6 U/h, well below 12 U/h ceiling). max_iob_units=25 U: Appropriate for estimated TDD ~20 U/day. Highest observed IOB is 5.9 U (Aug 21), 24% of max, not approaching limit. No changes needed. Note: High IOB on Aug 21 suggests meal was very large or sensor accuracy was compromised (new sensor placed 09:08 same day). Confirm accuracy before making IOB-limit changes.

autosens_enabled=false: Disabled appropriately. Autosens would track long-term sensitivity trend and adjust basal/ISF, but 14-day observation is short and GLP-1 introduction (Aug 14 onward) introduces acute sensitivity change that Autosens would lag. Keep disabled for now; can re-enable after 4–6 weeks of stable glucose control post-GLP-1 initiation. dynamic_sensitivity_enabled=true: Enabled and active. loop_status records show variable_sens ranging 27–95 across 24 events, confirming dynamic ISF adjustment is protecting against overcorrection when IOB is high (variable_sens lowered 50–75% at IOB >4 U) and allowing larger corrections when IOB is low (variable_sens raised 48–70% at IOB <0.5 U). This is protective and functioning correctly. dynamic_isf_adjustment_factor_percent=70: Standard oref1 default; no change needed. Overall sensitivity configuration is appropriate for current stage (short-term dynamic ISF, no long-term Autosens).

min_5m_carbimpact=8 mg/dL/5 min: Standard oref1 threshold. Glucose rise of ≥8 mg/dL/5 min is interpreted by UAM as meal carb activity and triggers COB accumulation. Observed post-bolus glucose patterns (Category B: rise 120–180 min post-bolus) are consistent with this threshold detecting meal carbs. No change needed. meal_max_absorption_hours=7: Standard oref1 default, slightly permissive (allows 7-hour absorption). Observed post-bolus glucose persistence (120–240 min elevated, some rebound at 240m suggesting continued absorption) is consistent with 4–6 hour typical absorption, well within 7-hour max. No change needed. Note: No e-carbs are declared (extended_carb_entries=0); all meals are treated as unannounced (UAM-detected) with fixed 7-hour max. Once carb logging begins, user can optionally declare e-carbs for slow-absorbing meals (e.g., high-fat combos) with custom duration (e.g., 4–5 hours for mixed, 2–3 hours for refined). This is deferred until after initial carb-logging phase.

ISF is globally 56 mg/dL/U (single segment at 00:00, applies 24/7). Variance is likely from SMB stacking and unrecorded meals, not from true ISF variability at the moment of bolus. After meal logging is active, ISF can be re-assessed. For now, keep 56 U/h. Note: time-of-day ISF segmentation (e.g., 45 mg/dL/U at 08:00 if dawn phenomenon is strong) could be considered if Autosens reveals systematic sensitivity variation, but is not recommended without meal logging to ground the adjustment.
Overnight target 90 mg/dL is appropriate. Hour 00–07 local achieve 88–98% TIR with average glucose 93–110 mg/dL. Target is appropriate. Keep as-is.

Late night target returns to 90 mg/dL (lower than daytime 100). Hour 22–23 local show 86–88% TIR with average 105–127 mg/dL, slightly above target. Basal handling this segment is appropriate (hours 21–23 show smooth transition into overnight). Keep target at 90 mg/dL.

DIA 10 hours is typical for rapid-acting insulins and is consistent with therapy response windows showing glucose changes over 60–360 min. Aug 15 11:25:37Z bolus at 181 mg/dL → 94 at 120 min → recovery over 360 min is consistent with 10-hour DIA. Do not change. If evening lows persist after meal bolus strategy is implemented, reassess whether DIA could be shortened (e.g., to 5–6 hours) to reduce SMB overlap; but this is a lower-priority change and should only be considered if other measures fail.

SMB and UAM are appropriately enabled. Both are functioning (loop statuses show SMB and UAM boosts active; temp basals 2–4 U/h observed). Problem is not with these features being on, but with user's meal bolus strategy being insufficient (2–4% of required, reactive). Enabling SMB/UAM is correct; the issue is user reliance on them. After meal bolus strategy is implemented (prebolus + carb logging), SMB/UAM will continue to fine-tune, but with less burden. Keep both enabled.

SMB activation conditions are appropriate. smb_always_enabled=true means SMB is active whenever carbs are detected (via UAM) or glucose is rising, which is correct for unannounced meals. smb_with_temp_target_enabled=true means SMB is active when temp target is set, which is appropriate (multiple temp targets observed in representative_events at 135 mg/dL, appropriately gating SMB). smb_with_high_temp_target_enabled=false prevents SMB during high temp targets, which is safety-appropriate. Keep all settings as-is.

current_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
suggested_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
rationale: SMB frequency (3 min) and sizing (15–20 min of basal) are standard for oref1 and appropriate for aggressive meal handling. Temporal stacking occurs due to combination of 3-min interval + 10-hour DIA + no carb logging (AAPS cannot track which insulin is meal-coverage vs. basal). However, this is not solved by reducing SMB frequency (that would reduce ability to handle meals, worsening afternoon hyperglycemia). Instead, implement meal logging and prebolus to reduce SMB burden (less meal insulin needed from SMB because user will provide it). Keep settings as-is now; if evening lows persist after meal strategy change, revisit SMB delivery parameters.

suggested_value: max_basal_u_per_hour=12 U/h; max_iob_units=25 U (keep now, plan reduction if needed)
rationale: max_basal_u_per_hour=12 U/h is standard and safe; observed temp basals (3–4 U/h) are well below this limit. No change needed. max_iob_units=25 U is high (typical 3–8 U) and permits temporal stacking, but the problem is timing not absolute IOB. Observed IOB peaks at 5.9 U, well below 25 U. Lowering max_iob would force tighter SMB spacing but would not solve afternoon hyperglycemia (would worsen it by restricting SMB). Instead, implement meal logging and prebolus to reduce meal bolus burden on SMB. After meal strategy is active for 5+ days, if evening lows persist at >10% time below range, consider reducing max_iob from 25 to 8–10 U as a trial. Keep at 25 U for now.

suggested_value: autosens_enabled=true (for diagnostic); dynamic_sensitivity_enabled=true; autosens_raises_target=false; autosens_lowers_target=false; dynamic_isf_adjustment_factor_percent=70 %
rationale: Autosens is currently disabled (autosens_enabled=false). Therapy response variance (CoV 32.6%, paradoxes −34 to −178 mg/dL) suggests either ISF miscalibration or sensitivity variability. Autosens could help diagnose. Recommendation: Enable Autosens with target adjustments disabled (autosens_raises_target=false, autosens_lowers_target=false) for 7 days as a diagnostic test. This allows ISF/CR to auto-adjust internally without changing glucose targets. Observe sensitivity_ratio values in loop statuses. If near 1.0, sensitivity is stable; if trending, ISF is miscalibrated. After diagnostic period, disable again if not needed. **Timing: Implement after meal_bolus_strategy is active for 5+ days to avoid confounding sensitivity learning with meal underbolusing.** Dynamic ISF 70% adjustment factor is appropriate and not a priority change. Keep as-is.

suggested_value: min_5m_carbimpact=10–12 mg/dL/5 min (if testing after meal logging); meal_max_absorption_hours=7 h
rationale: min_5m_carbimpact=8 mg/dL/5 min is conservative and appropriate for slow-absorption meals. However, observed deltas up to 4.83 mg/dL/min (Aug 18) imply true carb impact 15–20 mg/dL/5 min for high-glycemic meals, causing UAM to underestimate COB by ~47% and resulting in insufficient temp basal and hyperglycemia (peaks 280–293 mg/dL). Increasing min_5m_carbimpact to 10–12 without meal logging risks overcorrecting slow meals. Recommendation: (1) Implement meal logging first (7+ days). (2) With logged carbs, AAPS can calibrate UAM from actual meal absorption and internal Autosens. (3) If afternoon hyperglycemia persists, increase min_5m_carbimpact from 8 to 10 mg/dL/5 min as a trial (3 days). (4) If overcorrection of slow meals occurs, reduce to 8–10. **Decision: verify**—the value is present (8) but change is conditional on meal logging providing ground truth. meal_max_absorption_hours=7 h is appropriate and typical; keep as-is.

Nocturnal basal 0.6 U/h (lowest of day) is appropriate for overnight fasting. Fasting control 04:00-06:00 is excellent (TIR 95-98%), proving basal does not cause global overnight lows. Retain current value; verify stability 3-5 days before considering any change. Nocturnal lows are meal-driven, not basal-driven.

Early morning basal increase from 0.6 to 0.7 U/h at 05:00 aligns with dawn phenomenon transition. TIR 97.5% at hour_local=5 (04:00-05:00 UTC) and TIR 98.7% at hour_local=6 (05:00-06:00 UTC) confirm this segment is well-calibrated for pre-breakfast fasting. Retain.

Hour 08:00-11:00 post-breakfast shows TAR 8.9-20.2%, but this is meal-carb-driven (reactive bolus inadequate for meal size if carbs were logged), not basal-driven (basal at 06:00 does not cause 60-90 min delay to post-breakfast peak). Retain.
Midday basal 0.7 U/h continues through breakfast-to-lunch window. Post-breakfast TAR recovery to ~100 mg/dL by hour 11:00 suggests basal is not excessive for this segment. Retain.

Afternoon basal decrease to 0.5 U/h at 16:00 (lowest of day) coincides with lunch-to-afternoon window. TAR peak at hour_local=16 (15:00 UTC = 14:00-15:00 local) shows 32.1% above range, but this is during active lunch window with bolus insufficient for meal size; basal rate is low (0.5 U/h), ruling out basal as cause. Persistent lunch TAR 14-32% daily is meal-bolus-timing issue, not basal excess. Retain; reassess only if lunch TAR persists after pre-bolus is enabled and CR is validated (unlikely to need basal change).

Evening basal 0.6 U/h at 18:00 covers post-dinner window. Hour 21:00 (20:00 local) shows TIR 92.3%, indicating dinner is well-controlled. Evening overshoot into lows at 18:00-20:00 is correction-bolus-driven (bolus + ongoing SMB accumulate IOB), not basal-driven (basal rate is modest 0.6 U/h). Retain.

Evening basal increase to 0.7 U/h at 19:00 prepares for overnight fasting. Combined with 00:00 basal of 0.6 U/h, overnight profile transitions smoothly. TBR at 00:00-01:00 is not basal-driven; it is carb-absorption-timing + SMB stacking. Retain.
Overnight CR 13 g/U is baseline; no meal data to validate. Retain pending carb logging. After carb logging, if overnight snacks are logged, validate this value.
Early-morning CR 11.1 g/U (more aggressive than baseline 13 g/U) is plausible for pre-breakfast sensitivity window. No meal data to validate (fasting period, no meals 04:00-08:00). Retain.

Breakfast CR 13.2 g/U is reasonable baseline. Post-breakfast TAR 20.2% suggests meal boluses are small (0.1-0.25 U), but without logged carbs, cannot assess whether CR is correct or bolus is reactively undersized (UAM-only mode). Retain pending carb logging. After carb logging, if breakfast boluses are consistently smaller than expected (calculated_bolus = logged_carbs / 13.2), lower CR to 12.0-12.5 g/U. If consistently larger than expected, raise CR.

Lunch CR 10.5 g/U (most aggressive, lower than other segments) is plausible for afternoon sensitivity window. Persistent lunch TAR 14-32% suggests boluses are insufficient, but root cause is likely reactive lag (15-30 min delay from meal consumption to insulin injection) and meal size unknown. CR cannot be validated without meal carbs. Retain now; after carb logging stabilizes (5-7 days) and pre-bolus is enabled, monitor lunch TAR. If TAR persists >20%, test CR reduction (from 10.5 to 10.0 or 9.5 g/U, more aggressive) in isolation, monitoring 3-5 days for overshoot risk. Do not change CR and basal together.

Evening CR 12.6 g/U is between breakfast (13.2) and overnight (13.0). Post-dinner TIR 92.3% suggests dinner is well-controlled; bolus 0.45 U at 142 mg/dL followed by moderate peak recovery. Retain; validate after carb logging.

ISF 56 mg/dL/U is declared flat (no time segmentation) and scaled by Dynamic ISF 70% in real-time (baseline effective ISF = 56 × sensitivity_ratio × 0.70; at sensitivity_ratio=1.0, effective ISF ≈ 39.2 mg/dL/U; at sensitivity_ratio=0.8, effective ISF ≈ 31.4 mg/dL/U). Flat ISF profile is appropriate; real-time scaling via Dynamic ISF provides time-of-day adjustment. Retain; verify after carb logging by comparing predicted ISF (56 × logged_carbs, 10-hour DIA) to observed glucose response in therapy windows with minimal IOB.

Evening correction overshoot (bolus + ongoing SMB cause IOB stacking) is not a DIA error; it is a max_iob limit issue in context of aggressive SMB. Retain DIA 10h; if overshoot persists after stabilizing meal strategy, reassess max_iob (separate parameter).

Both SMB and UAM are appropriately enabled for reactive meal detection in absence of carb logging. Disabling either would remove the system's only meal-response mechanism. Once carb logging is enabled, reassess whether smb_with_cob_enabled should be changed from false to true (related group: automation_smb_uam). Retain current values.

suggested_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min [keep for now]; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min [keep for now]; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min [keep for now]

However, high max_iob may be intentional safety buffer for reactive UAM system (prevents system from withholding SMB due to IOB ceiling during meal windows). Retain max_iob 25 U until basal is stable and carb logging is active; then test reduction to 15-17 U, monitoring for overshoot reduction or meal-response sluggishness. Do not change max_iob and SMB interval together; change max_iob first if evening lows persist, or SMB interval if lunch TAR worsens.

Both settings are foundational for UAM operation; retain. After carb logging is enabled, these parameters remain relevant for UAM backup (if carb entry fails, UAM still detects meal via glucose rise).

CR 12.6g/U (20:00-00:00, evening/dinner window). Evening hyperglycemia not prominent (hours 20-23: avg 105-127mg/dL, mostly on-target). Keep unchanged; no evidence of insufficiency.

Reducing to 5-6h will halve IOB carryover into predawn, eliminating the low cluster without affecting meal hyperglycemia (which is meal-driven, not DIA-driven). Enabling Autosens now would not fix the problem. Dynamic ISF enabled at 70% factor is appropriate and conservative; allows real-time BG deviation adjustment while dampening overshoot. min_5m_carbimpact=8 is appropriate fallback assumption (system assumes minimum 8mg/dL/5min glucose rise from unaccounted carbs if COB estimate is low). autosens_enabled false and other autosens-related flags are appropriate (user relies on real-time Dynamic ISF, not time-history tracking). dynamic_sensitivity_enabled true is essential for real-time ISF adjustment. This change provides safety margin for GLP-1 increased sensitivity (user dosed 08-14, 08-17, 08-20) and meal-detection delays (min_5m_carbimpact 8 slows UAM activation, loop compensates with aggressive Dynamic ISF, creating oscillation). Reducing to 50% dampens oscillation without sacrificing real-time responsiveness.

Increasing meal_max_absorption_hours to 10h aligns with DIA, extends COB window, and gates SMB suppression through entire meal-insulin overlap. Expected benefit: reduction of evening/overnight lows by 3–5 percentage points within 7–14 days. Change requires carb logging to be effective (COB must be > 0 for gating).

SMB (Super Micro Bolus) and UAM (Unannounced Meal) are both enabled and are necessary for carb-less meal bolusing. Post-carb-logging, both remain enabled but their relative contribution shifts (immediate bolus + SMB/UAM split bolus instead of 100% SMB/UAM).

All settings are appropriate. Keep.

current_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
rationale: SMB delivery parameters are standard and proportional: (1) smb_interval_minutes=3 is aggressive (SMB fires every 3 min if conditions are met); standard in AAPS/oref1; not excessive given user's basal rates (0.6–0.8 U/h, max ~3 U/h equivalent per 3-min interval). (2) max_smb_basal_minutes=15 caps SMB at 15 min of current basal rate (e.g., with basal 0.7 U/h, max SMB ≈ 0.175 U per 3-min interval); prevents unbounded bolus. (3) max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 increases cap to 20 min when UAM detects meal (33% higher cap; justified to handle meal carbs quickly). All settings are within standard range. Representative treatments show frequent micro-boluses (3–5 min intervals), confirming SMB is active and delivering appropriate volumes. No issues observed. Keep. Post-carb-logging, SMB interval could be increased to 5 min (less frequent, smoother response) if glucose becomes very stable, but not necessary.

Safety limits are conservative: (1) max_basal_u_per_hour=12 U/h (observed max temp basal 4 U/h at 2026-08-14 18:40; 3× safety margin). (2) max_iob_units=25 U (observed peak IOB 5.935 U at 2026-08-21 21:09; 4.2× safety margin). Neither limit is being hit as a constraint on insulin delivery. No issues observed. Keep.

Sensitivity settings are appropriate: (1) autosens_enabled=false is correct; enabling Autosens without carb logging would loosen ISF further in high-glucose states (carb-driven elevation would trigger Autosens to assume insulin resistance, worsening glycemic variability). (2) dynamic_sensitivity_enabled=true is necessary; Dynamic ISF adapts ISF each loop cycle (observed 2.4–6.9 range) to protect against extremes. (3) autosens_raises_target=false and autosens_lowers_target=false are appropriate (Autosens is disabled; these are inactive). (4) dynamic_isf_adjustment_factor_percent=70% is moderate (narrow ISF range adjustment); allows ±30% adaptation, which is conservative. All settings are correct for carb-less operation. Keep. Post-carb-logging, if glucose stabilizes (CV drops from 32.6% to <25%), consider reducing adjustment factor to 50% for smoother response (optimization, not necessity).

Carb absorption parameters are plausible defaults: (1) min_5m_carbimpact=8 mg/dL/5 min is a threshold for UAM carb detection; when glucose accelerates >8 mg/dL/5 min, algorithm infers carbs and boosts SMB. Value is reasonable for typical meal response. (2) meal_max_absorption_hours=7 h is the maximum carb absorption time; allows algorithm to estimate COB decay over 7 hours. Values are appropriate for standard meals. However, cannot optimize without carbohydrate logging. Recommend: keep for now; post-carb-logging, if algorithm consistently underestimates carbs (frequent hyperglycemia despite boluses), increase min_5m_carbimpact to 10–12 mg/dL/5 min (higher threshold, requires stronger glucose acceleration to trigger UAM). If algorithm overestimates (frequent hypoglycemia despite meal presence), decrease to 6 mg/dL/5 min. For now, keep.

Afternoon CR 10.5 g/U (tightest, most sensitive hour). Directionally correct for peak afternoon sensitivity. However, afternoon hyperglycemia (14:00-16:00 BST, peak TAR 32.1%) suggests either CR 10.5 is still too permissive (grams per unit too high) OR meal is larger than CR assumes OR meal is not prebolused (delivered reactively after BG already rising). Cannot separate without meal logging. Hypothesis: CR may need tightening to 10 g/U, but this is speculative without meal data. Recommend: keep CR 10.5 g/U until meal logging (3-5 days) confirms meal size and timing. Then calculate whether CR matches observed meal response. If meal ~40-50 g at 12:00-13:00 produces BG peak at 15:00-16:00, calculate implied CR (bolus given / carbs = g/U) and compare to profile 10.5. If calculated CR > profile (e.g., 11-12), meal is larger than profile assumes. If calculated CR ≈ profile, meal bolus timing (prebolus vs. reactive) is issue. If calculated CR < profile (e.g., 9-10), tighten CR as secondary change after early-morning basal/target resolved.

ISF flat at 56 mg/dL/U across all hours. Therapy response windows show high outcome variability (−178 to +77 mg/dL at 120 min), indicating uncertainty. Cannot confirm without fasting ISF test or meal logging revealing systematic error (e.g., all corrections cause lows → ISF too high). Recommendation: keep ISF 56 mg/dL/U for now; after meal logging (3-5 days), if outcome variability persists, perform fasting ISF test (skip breakfast, known insulin dose, measure BG change at 120 min). If test shows ISF ~40-50, lower profile ISF. If test shows ISF ~56, outcome variability is meal/IOB context (meal logging prevents).

Early-morning TBR 18.5% with avg 90.6 mg/dL and lows to 42 mg/dL indicates target 90 mg/dL is too tight overnight, combined with basal 0.6 U/h. Raise target from 90 to 95 mg/dL OR lower basal from 0.6 to 0.5 U/h (or both, sequentially). Rationale for target change: safer overnight margin (95 reduces hypoglycemia risk without requiring basal change). Rationale for basal change: more conservative (maintains target intent, reduces basal contribution). Recommendation: test one change at a time. If changing target first: raise to 95 mg/dL, observe 3-5 nights. If changing basal first: lower to 0.5 U/h, observe same. Target 95 is acceptable overnight (looser than daytime 100); basal 0.5 is lower but supported by modest expected basal contribution (e.g., fasting overnight). Choose based on user preference: if user accepts higher overnight target, raise target; if user prefers aggressive basal, lower basal. Effect should be similar (reduce overnight insulin delivery). Monitor TBR and avoid lows <70 mg/dL.
Daytime target 100 mg/dL is appropriate; hours 08-16 (local) show variable TIR (67-98%) but target 100 is reasonable midpoint. No change recommended.

current_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
rationale: SMB frequency 3 min is aggressive but appropriate for closed-loop reactive strategy. max_smb_basal_minutes=15 means max SMB ≈0.175 U at 0.7 U/h basal (or 0.175 at 0.6, etc. depending on hour). max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 allows slightly larger UAM SMBs. max_basal=12 U/h and max_iob=25 U are well-chosen and not constraining. Observed max basal 4 U/h (33% utilization) and peak IOB 5.935 U (24% utilization). Ample headroom for aggressive corrections without hitting limits. Keep both settings. No need to adjust unless IOB peak approaches 20 U (risk of accumulation) or max basal approaches 10 U/h (risk of excessive correction). Current observation: safe margins.

Autosens disabled; dynamic sensitivity enabled at 70%. Autosens (long-term sensitivity adaptation) disabled is acceptable for stable users; this period shows stability within daily windows (not progressive drift), so Autosens off is reasonable. Dynamic ISF enabled and reducing ISF during afternoon peaks (observed ISF 2-3 during high BG, rises), helping but not preventing hyperglycemia (suggests meal/basal primary issue, not sensitivity). 70% adjustment factor is conservative. Keep all settings. Do not enable Autosens or increase Dynamic ISF adjustment (>70%) until basal/CR/meal strategy are optimized; then reassess sensitivity trends.

min_5m_carbimpact=8 mg/dL/5 min is conservative; catches fast meals, may miss slow-absorbing (high fat/protein) meals. meal_max_absorption_hours=7 h is appropriate (typical meals absorbed 2-4 h, extended absorption up to 6-7 h with fat/protein). No e-carbs used; SMB every 3 min and DIA 10 h implicitly handle extended absorption via accumulated IOB. Keep settings. Note: when meal logging begins, if user frequently has high-fat meals causing slow BG rise (Δ <8 mg/dL/5 min initially, then sustained rise 4-6 h), consider lowering min_5m_carbimpact to 5-6 mg/dL/5 min to detect those meals (secondary change after basal/CR validated).
